items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: I used to go around to old man Allen's house. Son wasn't born then. And I used to go around.

ctx.x: Right across the street is the little double house back in the yard. That's where Eddie used to live. Eddie Vinson and Tom Alvin on one side. Oh I see. And I used to go down there and join them every day. They had the bass violin player they called Teep. And when I first come down there I could play the bass. I was a little bit of a fellow. But Tom wanted the cornet playing. He said, get your cornet. We'll all show you. And Eddie Vinson played a vowel trombone you know. And he drilled me through what we were…

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: Allen would go see him... 'I've got a band, you know, that'll see me. All right, Allen, you get the job.'

ctx.x: No, he didn't have no fun with Ron. He used to play for dancers mostly. And I tell you, he had to swell all because they used to sit down and make their own music. Just make up most of the whole program, the stuff they made up. And he used to have some dancers at that time. Quadrillion and lances. And he used to play shatters and zilting. And I said variety. And two steps, one steps. He used to play little rags too, and then he used to play sentimental music in the overtill. My father was a first class musician.…
Oh, tell about how old man Allen used to get jobs. Did you ever hear that story?

Yeah. Allen used to, yeah, you know, one of them societies, and the men would get some jobs, and the men would get sick, you know, it'd be low, you know. Allen would go see him, you know, go visit him. And if he just thought that man wasn't going to live like that, you know, he'd say, well, tell the family, the people, you know, if anything happened, just ring me up, let me know. See, I've got a band, you know, that'll see me. All right, Allen, you get the job. If anything happened to him, he'd come like one.…
